evidence.title: Export your website stats
evidence.text:
Here's how to export all the native data collected for a particular Plausible dashboard to date. This export method is slower, cannot be segmented and is best suited for data portability purposes. It also doesn't include any data that you imported from external sources.

1. Open your Sites page and click the **Settings** icon next to the website you'd like to export. This opens its site settings, even if its dashboard is locked
2. In the **Imports & Exports** section, find the **Export Data** panel and click on the **Export to CSV** button
3. Your export will be queued and we'll email you when it's ready for download. The email says how long the download link stays valid

### What the export contains

The ZIP file holds one CSV file per report: visitors, sources, pages, entry pages, exit pages, locations, devices, browsers, operating systems, custom events and custom properties. Each file has one row per day for each item, such as one row per page per day with the full page path, so you get a complete list of every page that was visited. Visitors are counted per day, so adding them up across days gives a higher number than your dashboard shows for that period. Pageviews and visits can be added up. Scroll depth and time on page are stored as totals with their own visits columns: for a page's average over a period, add up `total_scroll_depth` and divide it by the sum of `total_scroll_depth_visits`. The same goes for `total_time_on_page` (in seconds) and `total_time_on_page_visits`. The files use the same format as our CSV import, so you can import them into another Plausible site.

evidence.title: Export your website stats
evidence.text:
The ZIP file holds one CSV file per dashboard report: visitors, pages, entry pages, exit pages, channels, sources, referrers, UTM tags, countries, regions, cities, browsers, operating systems, devices, custom properties and conversions. All of them follow the date range and filters you selected.

The visitors file follows the interval of your top chart, such as one row per day. The other files hold totals for the whole date range, with one row per page, source and so on. To keep the export quick, each of these files has the top 300 entries, and the pages and exit pages files have the top 100. For a full data export, refer to the instructions below.

Tip:
If you exported data for outbound link clicks, file downloads or 404 errors and want details like URLs, visitors, events and conversion rates, check the "custom_props.csv" file. The "conversions.csv" file only shows summary data.

You can open these CSV files in Excel or other data analysis tools.

question: ive set up my caddy config for the proxy, what do i change in my sites script tag now

answer: After configuring your Caddyfile, you should update the script tag on your site to the following: [1] ```html <script async src="/js/script.js"></script> <script> window.plausible=window.plausible||function(){(plausible.q=plausible.q||[]).push(arguments)},plausible.init=plausible.init||function(i){plausible.o=i||{}}; plausible.init({ endpoint: "/api/event" }) </script> ```

evidence.title: Proxying Plausible through Caddy
evidence.text:
With the above config in place, you can change the script tag on your site as follows:

```html
<script async src="/js/script.js"></script>
<script>
  window.plausible=window.plausible||function(){(plausible.q=plausible.q||[]).push(arguments)},plausible.init=plausible.init||function(i){plausible.o=i||{}};
  plausible.init({
    endpoint: "/api/event"
  })
</script>
```

question: I send a purchase event but the revenue column in my dashboard is empty. What should I check?
reference_answer: Check that the goal name in your site settings matches the event name exactly (case-sensitive) and that the `revenue` object has the right format, such as `{currency: 'USD', amount: 49.00}` with the amount in the main currency unit, not cents. Also use the Network tab to verify the event is sent with the revenue data, and make sure the currency code is a valid uppercase ISO 4217 code.

Use your browser's Network tab to confirm the event is being sent to plausible.io/api/event and that the payload includes the revenue data [1]. 4. If you are using a proxy, confirm it is correctly forwarding the full event payload [1]. 5. Ensure you are using standard uppercase ISO 4217 currency codes, as incorrect or lowercase codes will result in the event being recorded without revenue data [1].

evidence.title: Ecommerce revenue and attribution tracking
evidence.text:
**Revenue not showing in the dashboard**

- Check that the goal name in your Plausible site settings matches the event name exactly (case-sensitive)
- Confirm the `revenue` object uses the correct format: `{currency: 'USD', amount: 49.00}`. The amount can be a number or a numeric string (`49.00` or `"49.00"`). It must be in the main currency unit, not cents
- Use your browser's Network tab to verify the event is being sent. Look for a request to `plausible.io/api/event` and check the payload includes the revenue data
- If you are using a proxy, confirm the proxied endpoint is receiving and forwarding the full event payload

**Revenue amount is wrong**

- Check that the amount is in the major currency unit (49.00 for $49, not 4900 for cents)
- Stripe, Lemon Squeezy and Polar give amounts in cents. Divide by 100, except for zero-decimal currencies such as JPY. Paddle.js already gives the main unit
- If you see duplicate revenue, check for multiple Plausible snippets on the page or the event firing more than once on page load. See how to count each purchase only once
- For multi-currency stores, send each purchase’s actual amount and currency. Plausible automatically converts the amount into the goal’s reporting currency for total and average revenue.

**Currency code format**

Use standard ISO 4217 codes: USD, EUR, GBP, SEK and so on. Incorrect codes will cause the event to be recorded without revenue data. Codes must be uppercase. Stripe returns lowercase codes (`eur`), so convert them with `.toUpperCase()`. An invalid code doesn't return an error.

question: I finished the SAML setup on the identity provider side but people still can't log in through SSO

answer: Even if SAML is fully configured, SSO will not work until you add at least one domain and verify its ownership [1]. Go to the Configuration section of Single Sign-On under Team settings and click Start Configuring [2]. 2. Enter your identity provider's SSO URL, Entity ID, and Signing Certificate, then click Save [2]. 3. Enter the domain name used in email addresses of identities that should be allowed to log in and click Add Domain [2]. 4. Verify ownership of the domain by adding the displayed DNS TXT record, publishing the verification file or route, or adding the HTML meta tag [2]. 5. evidence.title: Single Sign-On (SSO)
evidence.text:
Before it's possible to log in through SSO, you need to add at least one domain and verify its ownership using one of the three available methods. SSO will not work until a domain is added and verified, even if SAML is fully configured.

When someone tries to log in via SSO, Plausible checks the domain part of their email address (the part after the “@”) against your configured domains. If a match is found, the user is redirected to the appropriate identity provider for authentication.

The ownership of every added domain must be verified using one of three methods:

- Adding a TXT DNS record to the root domain
- Publishing a file or exposing a route from the web page under the domain
- Adding a META HTML tag to the web page under the domain

Plausible SSO domain verification instructions with Run Verification Now

Once started, the verification process is retried in the background over the following hours until it succeeds. Once it's verified or fails after too many attempts, you will be notified by email. Verification can be immediately retried by canceling the running process and kicking off verification again.

Plausible SSO domains table with Cancel for an ongoing verification

### DNS Record Verification

A DNS record of type TXT must be configured for the root domain with `plausible-sso-verification=<domain identifier>` for content. DNS record update takes some time and verification might have to be retried a couple times before it succeeds.

The record is only checked during the verification process itself. Once the domain is verified, we don't check the record again, so you're free to remove it. Leaving it in place is harmless and means the domain can be re-verified without touching DNS again if you ever remove and re-add it. The same applies to the file, route and META tag verification methods below.
